elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1 retained: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed... The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." No unlimited-Customer-liability language remains.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.1: "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." Uses lowercase "fees" (not the narrow defined "Fees" = USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) and drops the "first Order Form" restriction; basis, temporal anchor (preceding the claim) and floor all match.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.2 unchanged: "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill."

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 "Excluded Claims" includes "a Party's breach of confidentiality... obligations"; 21.1 caps liability "Except for Excluded Claims."

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations" within Excluded Claims.
21.3: "its indemnification obligations" listed as an Excluded Claim.
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.
21.3: "...wilful misconduct, or fraud" within Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" within Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Rendered final sentence of 21.3: "Customer's payment obligations under this Agreement and any Order Form are not damages subject to the cap in this Section." This replaces the prior sentence limited to "undisputed Fees for conforming Services", which covered only the narrow defined Fees subset and would not have met the element.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability... The cap is mutual."

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 21.1 as rendered measures the cap on fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, with a USD 1,000,000 floor; the illusory USD 12,000 defined-Fees / first-Order-Form basis is removed.
21.3 Excluded Claims include "its indemnification obligations"; 21.1 opens "Except for Excluded Claims."

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims include breach of confidentiality obligations.

reasons: Deviation call is correct: as drafted the cap resolved to the defined "Fees" (USD 12,000 one-time Implementation Fee) under the first Order Form only, i.e. below six months' fees and in walk-away territory, notwithstanding the otherwise complete mutual carve-out set.

Both operations are surgical. Operation 1 rewrites only the cap measure in 21.1 and retains the favourable mutuality sentence; operation 2 replaces only the narrow payment sentence in 21.3, which was necessary because "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" excludes only a narrowly defined subset of Fees rather than Customer payment obligations as a whole.

No extras were added: no survival tail, no procedure, no additional damages categories; 21.2 (including the Customer-favourable direct-damages characterisation of restoration, replacement services, notice and incident-response costs) is left verbatim, and the 1.5/1.6 definitions are untouched so no cross-reference is orphaned.

Drafting-hygiene note (not a failure): 21.1 relies on lowercase "fees" to escape the capitalised "Fees" definition. Because "Fees" remains defined as the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee, consider adding a short parenthetical such as "(all amounts payable by Customer for Services, regardless of the definition of 'Fees')" only if the counterparty argues the defined term governs — as rendered the capitalisation convention is sufficient and adding it now would risk non-minimality.

Preferred level is complete, so no fallback fallback-only redline is needed; the comment correctly states the position and that indemnities, confidentiality, data protection and security sit outside the cap.
